blocks.text: Spicers is a subculture in Ireland, primarily located around Dublin, Ireland during the late 2000s to the early 2010s. It is characterized by Adidas tracksuits, elaborate mullets, neon/tacky outfits, dubstep, and an online life that was based on social media platforms such as Bebo. The Spicer style appearance was distinct, loud, and instantly recognizable in suburban areas such as Swords, Lucan, Malahide, and Raheny.
The Haircut: Heavily dyed hair and straightened mullets were standard, with the hair straightener serving as a tool.
The Wardrobe: Outfits featured heavily on shutter shades, skinny jeans, Adidas tracksuits, and graphic tees.
Electric Music: Spicers favored genres like jumpstyle, hardstyle, and dubstep, often techno shuffling that is often practiced among groups.
Bebo was the major digital home among the Spicers community.
Profile Customization: Users spent hours embedding custom homepage backgrounds, frequently inspired by the teen television show Skins.
Social Hierarchy: Drama and friendships emerged out through infamous Bebo's "Top 16" friends feature publicly.
Music and Flashboxes: Profiles featured stylized text and auto-playing DJ Cami tracks.
